children: By Megan Cheah
A consortium led by consumer-focused investment firm L Catterton is buying a majority stake in athletic competition Hyrox from Infront Sports & Media.
L Catterton, backed by fashion company LVMH, is making the investment alongside Hyrox founders Christian Toetzke and Moritz Furste, and venture-capital firm WndrCo, Infront said Tuesday.
The deal could value Hyrox at around 600 million euros, equivalent to $697.5 million, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

Hyrox, which held its first edition in Germany in 2018, combines a series of workout challenges into a hybrid race. Exercises in the competition are similar to those found in athletic gyms, such as burpee broad jumps and sandbag lunges.
Over the 2025-2026 season, Hyrox held more than 100 events that attracted more than 1.4 million participants, said Infront.
Greenwich, Conn.-based L Catterton sees Hyrox as "uniquely well positioned" in creating a global movement centering on fitness, said managing director Shena Willis.
The firm, which manages around $40 billion of assets, has made more than 300 investments in consumer companies, including sandal maker Birkenstock.
Hyrox founder Toetzke said it aims to focus on its Olympics aspirations, grow its participants and invest in new products that enhance Hyrox's offering.

Infront became the majority owner of Hyrox in October 2022. The divestment of its stake comes after the Swiss marketing and media company conducted a strategic review, said Infront President and Chief Executive Philippe Blatter.
